output.brief:
The buffering in Kestria is not caused by the new CDN. It comes from the smart-TV app 5.2 release. That release lowered the player's startup buffer from 10 s to 4 s and let it switch up in quality after 2 s of buffering. It went live in Kestria first, on 9 October, the same day as the CDN cutover. In 12–25 October data, smart-TV 5.2 stalls 5.9% of viewing time. Every other client on Tessaline, including the web player, the mobile apps and smart-TV 5.1, stays at 0.6–0.7%. The gap is the same on all three ISPs. Employee TVs on Corvane showed the same problem before launch (5.7% versus 0.6%), and the issue was deferred. Handball viewing does not explain it, because stalls were flat on match nights.

What to do: reject the SLA notice, fee withholding and switch back. Revert Kestria to the 5.1 streaming settings (abr_v2 remote config, effective in about an hour). Hold the 20 November all-market rollout until it is fixed. Keep the alert on. Don't give free months yet. The October price rise is a rival explanation for the extra cancellations. Add app-version breakdowns to the dashboard when the pipeline allows.
